author: aobolensk
title: JS API E2E test cleanup fails - Permission denied removing d3dcompiler_47.dll on Windows
signature: rm cannot remove electron.exe Permission denied|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: JS API (22)
failed_jobs.symptom: E2E after-all cleanup hook fails: rm cannot remove d3dcompiler_47.dll - Permission denied

key_errors:
exec error: Error: Command failed: rm -rf demo-electron-app-project
rm: cannot remove 'demo-electron-app-project/node_modules/electron/dist/d3dcompiler_47.dll': Permission denied
1) "after all" hook for "should run electron package and verify output": Error: Command failed: rm -rf demo-electron-app-project
root_cause: The E2E test for the openvino-node Electron integration passes successfully (2 tests pass), but the Mocha 'after all' cleanup hook fails when attempting to remove the test directory using 'rm -rf'. On Windows, the Electron binary locks d3dcompiler_47.dll and other DLLs via file handles that persist briefly after the process exits. The rm command fails with EACCES/Permission denied because the Windows OS still holds a lock on the file. This is a Windows runner environment issue unrelated to the PR changes (which only touch Snippets buffer allocation code).
reproduction_steps: Run the JS API E2E test on a Windows runner immediately after an Electron process exits; the cleanup may fail due to DLL file locks.
recommended_actions: Use a retry-loop or delayed rm in the E2E after-all hook instead of a plain rm -rf call
Use rimraf or a Windows-compatible file removal utility that handles locked files
Add a short sleep before cleanup to allow Windows to release file handles
Consider using the 'force' option or robocopy /MIR for cleanup on Windows runners
prevention_strategies: Use robust cleanup utilities (rimraf, robocopy) that handle locked DLL files on Windows. Add retry logic in the E2E test cleanup hooks.
historical_context: First recorded occurrence of this specific pattern. The failure is unrelated to the PR changes (Snippets buffer optimization).
